q: The counting argument for lower bounds on circuit complexity (Shannon, 1949) works by showing that most Boolean functions on n bits require circuits of size:
exp: Shannon counting argument: there are 2^{2^n} functions on n bits but only ≈ (nS)^S circuits of size S. For S ≪ 2^n/n, this is less than 2^{2^n}, so most functions require circuit size Ω(2^n/n). Despite this, no explicit function is known to require super-polynomial circuits.
